title: North Korea's October missile spree
deck: Pyongyang fired a hypersonic missile, two ballistic missiles and two submarine-launched cruise missiles in twelve days, just as Trump floated a November meeting with Kim and as Kim courted Beijing.

fuel.title: North Korea lodges UN letters against Seoul
fuel.how: A UN envoy accused South Korea of nuclear plans, which hardens the rhetoric and raises the price Pyongyang can ask for talks.

fuel.title: Artillery and howitzer reported near border
fuel.how: Reports of 122mm artillery and a spotted howitzer put a conventional threat to Seoul next to the missile tests.

fuel.title: Kim tours Dandong, touts Yalu River Bridge
fuel.how: A visit to a Chinese bus factory with strong North Korean ties and the new bridge, plus Beijing's 'unwavering policy' line, signals economic and diplomatic backing that lowers Pyongyang's cost of defiance.

card.headline: North Korea is raising its price for talks with missiles, and China is quietly backing its hand

keyNumber.label: flown by two ballistic missiles on 12 October, two days before the sub-launched cruise missile tests

forYou.line: Tests on this scale have not usually moved global markets for long. Watch Korean and Japanese assets for brief risk-off moves after each launch.
Launches off the east coast can trigger notices and rerouting near Korea and Japan. Expect short disruptions, not closures.
A first sub-launched cruise test since January 2024 shows a new sea-based strike option. South Korea and Japan will push for more missile defence.
The main question is whether Trump and Kim meet around his November Asia trip, and what Pyongyang demands first.

effects.text: Two types of sub-launched strategic cruise missiles fired off the east coast on 14 October, including a Pulhwasal-3-31
North Korea lodges letters with the UN and a UN envoy accuses Seoul of nuclear plans
Reports of 122mm artillery near the border and a spotted howitzer raise military tension
Kim tours Dandong and the new Yalu River Bridge; Beijing calls ties with Pyongyang an unwavering policy
Pyongyang's price for any Trump meeting rises; most Korean assessments are sceptical that Kim's China trip lays the ground for a summit
Seoul splits along party lines over how to respond to Kim's China visit; the Unification Ministry hopes it restarts dialogue
South Korea and Japan weigh more missile defence and surveillance against a sea-based launch option
Kim and Putin both angle for a Trump summit, so Korean and Ukraine diplomacy become linked bargaining chips
Beijing, as APEC host in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, holds more influence over both Trump's and Kim's agendas
Pressure on US allies in Northeast and Southeast Asia rises at the same time, with the Philippines at risk from Chinese pressure

whatHappened: On 14 October 2026, North Korea fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles off its east coast, state media said. One was a Pulhwasal-3-31. Reports say it was the first sub-launched cruise missile test since January 2024.

It capped a month of launches. A hypersonic intermediate-range missile flew on 3 October. Two ballistic missiles flew more than 560 miles on 12 October, days after South Korea's first hypersonic test and a DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

On 12 October Trump said he 'may' meet Kim Jong Un during his November Asia trip. Two days later came the sub-launched tests. By 26 October, Kim had visited the Chinese border city of Dandong, and North Korea had sent letters to the UN accusing Seoul of nuclear plans. Reports also described artillery near the border.
whyItMatters: Politics: Pyongyang is using launches to raise its price for talks. The UN letters accusing Seoul of nuclear plans harden the rhetoric at the same moment Trump hints at a meeting. Seoul's parties disagree on how to read Kim's China trip.

Security: a sea-based cruise missile is harder to track than one launched from a fixed site. Reports of 122mm artillery and a howitzer near the border add a conventional threat to Seoul on top of the missile tests. We have not checked those reports beyond the headlines.

Trade and shipping: Kim toured a Chinese bus factory with strong North Korean ties and highlighted the new Yalu River Bridge. Beijing said developing ties is an unwavering policy. That suggests economic and diplomatic backing, which lowers the cost to Pyongyang of defying pressure.

The timing matters. China hosts APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, and Trump says he may meet Kim on the trip. Kim and Putin are both angling for a Trump summit, and North Korea's troops-for-technology alliance with Moscow ties their bargaining together.

winners.why: The launches, the China visit and the Russia link all raise what Washington must offer to get a meeting.
As APEC host, it sits between Trump and Kim and can present itself as indispensable to both.

winners.who: Defence industries in South Korea and Japan
winners.why: Sea-based launches strengthen the case for missile defence and surveillance spending. This is our estimate, not a reported order.

losers.who: South Korean soldiers and border communities
losers.why: Three soldiers were wounded by a DMZ landmine blast, and reports of artillery near the border raise exposure.
The Unification Ministry hopes Kim's China trip restarts dialogue, but Pyongyang is accusing Seoul of nuclear plans at the UN.
Repeated launches in one month make a deal that freezes the programme harder to sell in Washington.

whatsNext: Late October: watch for further launches and for how Seoul and Tokyo respond to the artillery and UN letters.
November: Trump's Asia trip, with a possible Kim meeting still unconfirmed.
18-19 November: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, hosted by China.

options: More launches and no Trump-Kim meeting

predict.explanation: Our base case, about 40%, is more testing alongside talk of talks, with no confirmed meeting by the end of APEC. Most Korean assessments are sceptical that Kim's China trip prepares a US summit, and Pyongyang has just raised its price.

timeline.title: Previous reported sub-launched cruise missile test
timeline.detail: The 14 October 2026 test was described as the first of this kind since January 2024.

timeline.title: Xi's state visit to Washington ends
timeline.detail: The two sides declared a 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' but few concrete trade deliverables. This sets the diplomatic backdrop for November.

timeline.title: Hypersonic intermediate-range missile launched
timeline.detail: The first of the October launches reported by the sources.

timeline.title: Two ballistic missiles fly more than 560 miles
timeline.detail: Launched days after South Korea's first hypersonic test and a DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

timeline.title: Trump says he 'may' meet Kim in November
timeline.detail: He was speaking about his Asia trip, which includes the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

timeline.title: Sub-launched strategic cruise missiles fired
timeline.detail: Two types, including a Pulhwasal-3-31, off the east coast, per state media. The test came two days after Trump's remark.

timeline.title: Korean assessments doubt a summit link to Kim's China trip
timeline.detail: A Financial News piece says most assessments are sceptical that the visit was meant to lay the groundwork for a North Korea-US summit.

timeline.title: UN letters and a spotted howitzer
timeline.detail: A North Korean envoy accuses Seoul of nuclear plans; Asahi reports tensions are high with letters lodged at the UN and a howitzer spotted. Another outlet reports 122mm artillery near the border.

timeline.title: Kim tours Dandong and the new Yalu River Bridge
timeline.detail: He visited a Chinese bus factory with strong North Korean ties. Beijing called developing ties with Pyongyang an unwavering policy.

causes.name: Weapons programme
causes.detail: North Korea has long expanded ballistic, hypersonic and cruise missile options. The sub-launched cruise missile adds a sea-based route.

causes.name: Russia alignment
causes.detail: Pyongyang's troops-for-technology alliance with Moscow gives it a partner that does not push for restraint.

causes.name: Chinese backing
causes.detail: Beijing calls ties with Pyongyang an unwavering policy and a new Yalu River Bridge opens a trade link.

causes.name: Trump's remark
causes.detail: On 12 October he said he 'may' meet Kim on his November Asia trip. Pyongyang followed with launches two days later.

causes.name: South Korean hypersonic test
causes.detail: Seoul's first hypersonic test, days before 12 October, gave Pyongyang a pretext to show its own capability.

causes.name: DMZ landmine blast
causes.detail: Three South Korean soldiers were wounded, which raised border tension.

causes.name: UN and rhetoric fight
causes.detail: A North Korean envoy accused Seoul of nuclear plans and lodged letters with the UN.

causes.name: Artillery reports
causes.detail: Reports of 122mm artillery and a howitzer near the border keep pressure on Seoul.

stakeholders.name: Kim Jong Un
stakeholders.wants: Recognition, sanctions relief and a better price for any talks with Washington
stakeholders.leverage: A growing missile menu, Chinese and Russian backing, and the choice of when to meet Trump
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep testing, keep talks open, and let Beijing's APEC role set the stage.

stakeholders.name: Donald Trump
stakeholders.wants: A headline summit and a deal on the Korean programme without losing allies
stakeholders.leverage: The offer of a meeting, sanctions and the US alliance with Seoul and Tokyo
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep saying he 'may' meet Kim while avoiding commitments before Shenzhen.

stakeholders.name: Seoul government
stakeholders.wants: A lower threat on the border and a restart of dialogue
stakeholders.leverage: Its own military upgrades, such as the hypersonic test, and its alliance with Washington
stakeholders.likelyMove: Condemn tests, back US diplomacy and boost deterrence while the Unification Ministry pushes dialogue.

stakeholders.name: Xi Jinping and Beijing
stakeholders.role: APEC host and North Korea's main partner
stakeholders.wants: Stability, leverage over Washington and a role as broker
stakeholders.leverage: Trade, the Yalu River Bridge and the Shenzhen summit agenda
stakeholders.likelyMove: Present itself as essential to any Trump-Kim meeting while keeping ties with Pyongyang.

stakeholders.name: Vladimir Putin and Moscow
stakeholders.wants: His own Trump summit on Ukraine and continued troops-for-technology support
stakeholders.leverage: Technology and diplomatic cover for Pyongyang
stakeholders.likelyMove: Treat Kim's bargaining as linked to his own bid for talks with Trump and Xi.

stakeholders.name: Tokyo
stakeholders.leverage: Alliance with Washington and its own defence budget
stakeholders.likelyMove: Push for shared surveillance and protest tests that threaten its waters.

sectors.why: A sea-based cruise launch option adds to demand for tracking and interception in South Korea and Japan. This is our estimate.

sectors.sector: South Korean and Japanese defence industry
sectors.why: A hypersonic race and artillery on the border support spending, though no new orders are cited.

sectors.sector: China-North Korea border trade and logistics
sectors.why: Kim highlighted the new Yalu River Bridge at Dandong and Beijing called ties unwavering. Actual volumes are not in the material.
Launches usually bring brief risk-off moves that fade. The material gives no price data, so this is a judgement.

sectors.sector: Aviation and shipping near Korea and Japan
sectors.why: Launches off the east coast can lead to warnings and short rerouting. We have no reported disruption.
The summit window with Trump opens, but each launch raises the price and the risks of a failed meeting.

dailyLife.effect: Landmine blasts and reports of artillery near the DMZ raise safety concerns for soldiers and local residents.
Launches can bring short alerts and notices to aircraft and ships; no lasting disruption is reported.
Ruling and opposition parties disagree over Kim's China trip, so how the government responds will be a political fight at home.
No reported effect on prices so far. Spikes tend to be brief after launches; this is general knowledge, not a figure from the sources.

scenarios.name: Test-and-talk stalemate
scenarios.looksLike: More launches or rhetoric, talk about a Trump-Kim meeting, and no confirmed meeting by the end of APEC.
signposts: No announcement of a venue or date
Pyongyang repeats demands through the UN
scenarios.effectOnWorld: The risk stays elevated but contained; allies keep upgrading defence.

scenarios.name: Summit window opens
scenarios.looksLike: A Trump-Kim meeting is announced or held around his Asia trip, with Beijing and perhaps Moscow in supporting roles.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Headlines turn to diplomacy, but a thin deal would leave sanctions and the weapons programme largely unchanged.

scenarios.name: Border escalation
scenarios.looksLike: A clash on or near the DMZ after the landmine blast and artillery reports turns deadly, or a launch lands near Japan or South Korea.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Summit plans freeze, markets wobble and the US is drawn into crisis management.

scenarios.name: Quiet pause
scenarios.looksLike: Pyongyang stops launches and keeps its options open for the summit season, relying on Beijing's diplomacy.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Tensions fall for a time without a deal; the underlying programme keeps growing.

predictions.text: North Korea will fire at least one more missile before the APEC summit opens on 18 November (probability about 55%).
Trump and Kim will not hold a face-to-face meeting during the November Asia trip (probability about 75%).
No deaths result from a clash between the two Koreas (probability about 85%).
China will publicly call for restraint or dialogue on the peninsula around the APEC summit without criticising Pyongyang by name (probability about 80%).
North Korea will carry out another sub-launched missile test of any type by mid-2027 (probability about 50%).

actions: Review contingency plans for flights, shipping and staff in Korea and Japan around launch days.
Check exposure to border trade routes between China and North Korea and to sanctions rules.
Brief travelling staff on local alerts.
Treat launches as short-term volatility triggers unless they come with border fighting or casualties.
Watch the APEC dates and Trump's travel plans as the main catalysts.
Avoid assuming that a summit means sanctions relief; most Korean assessments are sceptical.
Follow official alerts if you live or travel near the DMZ or east coast.
Expect noise, not disruption, in prices and travel unless a clash occurs.
Keep Seoul, Tokyo and Washington aligned before November so Pyongyang cannot split them.
Press Beijing to use its APEC host role to restrain launches.
Prepare crisis channels on the DMZ after the landmine blast and artillery reports.

analogues.event: Missile tests followed by Trump-Kim diplomacy
analogues.whatFollowed: A year of heavy testing was followed by the June 2018 Singapore summit. It produced a joint statement but little lasting change in the weapons programme.
A second Trump-Kim meeting ended without a deal in February 2019 and talks stalled. It is a reminder that summits can fail when expectations differ.

analogues.event: Heavy missile testing during a diplomatic freeze
analogues.whatFollowed: North Korea launched an unusually large number of missiles while talks were stalled, with allies responding through exercises and defence upgrades.

watch.title: APEC leaders' meeting, Shenzhen (to 19 November)
watch.why: Trump plans to attend as China hosts. A Kim meeting would be tied to it.

watch.title: Trump's November Asia itinerary
watch.why: Any confirmed stop or venue for a Kim meeting would change the outlook.

watch.title: Further launches
watch.why: More tests, especially sub-launched or ballistic, would show Pyongyang is raising the price further.

watch.title: UN follow-up to North Korea's letters
watch.why: Watch whether the accusation of South Korean nuclear plans becomes a formal diplomatic campaign.

watch.title: Border artillery reports
watch.why: Confirmation of the 122mm artillery or live fire would raise the risk of a clash.

watch.title: Yalu River Bridge and Dandong trade
watch.why: Signs the bridge opens to traffic or that Beijing offers more support would show how far China is backing Pyongyang.

watch.title: Putin's summit push
watch.why: Kim and Putin are both angling for Trump meetings, so progress on Ukraine could shape the Korean track.

confidence.claim: Details of the 14 October sub-launched missile tests
confidence.note: Reported by Al Jazeera and Stars and Stripes, citing North Korean state media.

confidence.claim: The 3 October and 12 October launches, including the 560-mile flight
confidence.note: Taken from the event summary and the Stars and Stripes headline; we did not read the full text of every report.

confidence.claim: Reports of 122mm artillery and a howitzer near the border
confidence.note: Based on headlines only; the details and location are not verified.

confidence.claim: Kim's visit to Dandong and China's 'unwavering policy' line
confidence.note: Several Korean outlets carry the same story; dates and full itinerary are not confirmed in the headlines.

confidence.claim: The link between Trump's offer and the timing of the launches
confidence.note: The sequence is documented; any claim that one caused the other is an inference.

evidence.method: Drafted from the two cited sources on the event, 22 matched wire headlines (mostly Korean, Japanese and regional outlets from 25-26 October) and the connected event notes on APEC, Ukraine summit diplomacy and the South China Sea. Many headlines were read without the full text, so claims from them are hedged. Probabilities, scenarios and sector effects are our estimates; the material has no market or trade data, so none is quoted.
